signals.observation:
narrative: "_A summary of what Ken Rahjes has publicly said, posted, and amplified across campaign channels, public social metadata, official records, and credible indexed public coverage. Drawn from public captures of his campaign site, Facebook, X, Kansas Legislature records, PBS/Smoky Hills listings, Kansas Ag Report listings, Hays Post, and KVOE from 2016 through May 2026, with the campaign-period read centered on 2025 through May 11, 2026. We report patterns; we do not interpret intent._

Across the accessible public set, Rahjes' dominant campaign frame is a low-key administrative argument: secure elections, business services, trust, rural Kansas, and legislative experience. His campaign homepage presents him as "A family man, built from trust and integrity" and uses the slogan block "TRUST...BUT VERIFY" and "Securing Your Future with Trust and Integrity." ([source](https://kenforkansas.com/)) The same page routes supporters only to Facebook and X, saying, "Receive future updates from Ken on Facebook & X." ([source](https://kenforkansas.com/))

The clearest candidate-controlled secretary-of-state statement is the July 2025 filing post on his campaign site. Rahjes framed the office through business filings and election administration, saying Kansas should streamline business filings, improve the One Stop portal, continue security initiatives for election officials and poll workers, increase election-audit transparency, and produce fast, accurate results. In that post, he said, "We have many great assets in our state, but the best one is our people," and, "I will ensure Kansas will be a leader when it comes to election integrity and election security." ([source](https://kenforkansas.com/news/rahjes-files-for-secretary-of-state/))

Local coverage of his campaign stops repeats the same two-part argument. At a November 2025 Hays event, Rahjes said, "I believe I'm most effective by looking you in the eye and having a conversation," and tied his run to county clerks, voter ID, ending the three-day mail-ballot grace period, and civic education in schools. On the business side, he described the secretary of state's office as the "front door" for people trying to operate in Kansas and said, "let's make Kansas business-friendly again." ([source](https://hayspost.com/posts/d7c59a6a-6884-4ac9-aad1-7c9d728f5f5f))

His business-services message connects process reform to property-tax pressure. In Hays, Rahjes said he wanted entrepreneurs to avoid navigating multiple agencies and argued, "There's no greater solution than to grow our tax base. I firmly believe that if you grow the base, then you will lower the rate." ([source](https://hayspost.com/posts/d7c59a6a-6884-4ac9-aad1-7c9d728f5f5f)) KVOE's March 2026 Emporia coverage likewise reported that he wanted to continue Scott Schwab's work making life easier for business owners and entrepreneurs, while also stressing that voters want their votes counted and secure. ([source](https://kvoe.com/2026/03/16/rahjes-in-emporia-touting-secretary-of-state-bid/))

The social footprint is present but not especially broad. Public Facebook metadata captured on May 11, 2026 listed [Ken For Kansas](https://www.facebook.com/kenforkansas/) at 985 likes and 210 talking about this, with the page description identifying Rahjes as a Kansas Secretary of State candidate and Kansas House member. The campaign-linked X handle is [@kenrahjes](https://x.com/kenrahjes); Muck Rack indexes it as a personal account for a small-business owner, agriculture broadcaster, and Kansas state representative, with the note that retweets do not imply endorsement. ([source](https://muckrack.com/ken-rahjes)) Logged-out capture did not expose a reliable post-level Facebook or X feed, so the harvest does not claim post counts, repost networks, or post-level engagement.

Rahjes' public identity outside the campaign is heavily rural and agricultural. The Kansas Legislature profile lists him as House District 110, chair of Agriculture and Natural Resources, and a member of Appropriations, Agriculture and Natural Resources Budget, Joint Committee on Special Claims Against the State, and the Water Program Task Force. ([source](https://www.kslegislature.gov/b2025_26/legislators/rep_rahjes_ken_1/)) Kansas Ag Report identifies him as host of a weekly agriculture television show focused on issues important to Kansas farmers and ranchers, and Apple Podcasts lists Kansas Ag Report as a 109-episode business-news podcast active from 2021 to 2023. ([Kansas Ag Report](https://kansasagreport.net/about), [Apple Podcasts](https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/kansas-ag-report/id1551218249))

That rural frame also shows up in legislative coffees and issue coverage. In February 2026, Rahjes spoke about senior transportation, conservation, water, AI in campaigns, and NIL funding. On conservation and local control, he said, "Me living in Agra should not tell Wichita County what they should do with their kids. Johnson County shouldn't tell Hays how much water they should use, and Hays shouldn't tell Johnson County how green their yard should be." On water, he said, "If we don't have good conservation, which goes into water, then we're just dust." ([source](https://hayspost.com/posts/93f5e63a-dd1b-411a-98f8-c3ca8b2c187a))

His education and local-control language predates the secretary-of-state campaign and appears in local legislative coverage. In February 2025, Rahjes questioned the need for the U.S. Department of Education and said, "Wouldn't it be nice to have local school boards decide what's best for the local school children instead of having some edict from D.C. that says what works in Houston works in Ellis?" The same coverage records his support for limiting gender-transition procedures for minors and his comment that the issue applied to minors because of long-term consequences. ([source](https://hayspost.com/posts/c009ea47-7cfc-4c71-bad9-7dae18a389c6))

The reviewed set shows only limited direct engagement with national culture-war language. His campaign material uses "trust," "integrity," "security," "business-friendly," and rural stewardship more often than national partisan attack language. The accessible 2025-2026 campaign record did not show Rahjes attacking, tagging, or amplifying his Republican primary opponent Pat Proctor. It also did not show a meaningful candidate-controlled presence on Instagram, TikTok, Truth Social, Gab, Gettr, Substack, Reddit, or LinkedIn.

Several issue areas do not appear at meaningful frequency in the accessible material reviewed. The public set did not include repeated candidate-controlled posts centered on Medicaid expansion, child care, housing costs, broadband, veterans services, immigration, border policy, guns, crime, federal foreign policy, or abortion beyond the older 2021 Value Them Both legislative update. Gender-transition policy, rural health, senior transportation, AI campaign misuse, education, water, and conservation appear in local legislative coverage, but the dominant secretary-of-state campaign frame remains elections plus business services.

Methodology: Public capture was conducted on May 11, 2026. Date range covered: Nov. 8, 2016 to May 11, 2026 for public campaign-news archive and indexed public presence; campaign-period analysis emphasizes Feb. 9, 2025 to May 11, 2026. Platforms surveyed: campaign website, Facebook, X/Twitter, Instagram, LinkedIn, YouTube, PBS/Smoky Hills, Kansas Ag Report, Podbean, Apple Podcasts, Kansas Legislature, Hays Post, KVOE, Muck Rack, TikTok, Truth Social, Gab, Gettr, Substack, Reddit, and public search indexes. Items examined: 16 accessible original/profile/public-record/media items and 0 verified reposts. Login-walled or script-blocked material was not counted as reviewed. Engagement was reported only when visible in public metadata or indexed public listings on capture date. We report patterns; we do not interpret intent.",
signals.caveat: Observed online/social signal only; do not infer belief, endorsement, or policy position from this item alone.

signals.observation: Across the harvested public record on X ([@RealPatProctor](https://x.com/RealPatProctor)), Facebook ([@PatProctorKS](https://www.facebook.com/PatProctorKS/)), YouTube ([Pat Proctor for Kansas](https://www.youtube.com/@patproctorforkansas655)), and Instagram ([@patproctor4ks](https://www.instagram.com/patproctor4ks/)), Proctor's dominant topic is election administration. The same phrase recurs across every platform: his Instagram bio reads "Fighting to restore confidence in our elections," his Facebook page lists him as "fighting to restore confidence in our elections," and his April 2025 campaign-launch [YouTube video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8oGPhVyuYfs) opens with the line "Job one is restoring confidence in our elections." A second recurring frame is foreign money in Kansas elections. On May 6, 2025, Proctor posted on X: "The axis of ballot harvesting strikes again! Loudlight, Appleseed, and their allies hide behind their supposed nonpartisan, nonprofit status to rake in millions from George Soros and foreign billionaires that they use to sue every common sense measure we pass to restore…" ([source](https://x.com/RealPatProctor)). On May 27, 2025, he posted on X: "Why are the @aclukansas, Planned Parenthood, and the other members of the pro-abortion 'Kansans for Constitutional Freedom' suing to protect their ability to hide behind their nonprofit, supposedly 'non-partisan' status to rake in millions from foreign billionaires" ([source](https://x.com/RealPatProctor/status/1927386363806073212)).
signals.caveat: Candidate-controlled post or candidate-controlled platform statement; still use as stated/observed content, not inferred motive.

signals.observation: For the Leavenworth district itself, Proctor's local content is less voluminous than his statewide-elections content but is present. An October 5, 2025 [YouTube video](https://www.youtube.com/@patproctorforkansas655) addresses bringing jobs and opportunity back to Leavenworth. His campaign and legislative biographies foreground his co-ownership with his wife Aree of Baan Thai Restaurant in Leavenworth. The April 2025 [Wichita State University](https://www.kslegislature.gov/li/b2025_26/members/rep_proctor_pat_1/) listing identifies him as a college professor in addition to his House role. The harvested set does not contain Leavenworth-specific posts about Fort Leavenworth military-family issues, federal-prison employment, or city infrastructure at a frequency comparable to his statewide election-administration posts.
signals.caveat: Candidate-controlled post or candidate-controlled platform statement; still use as stated/observed content, not inferred motive.

signals.observation: Proctor's public alignment network on his own feed centers on Kansas Republican officeholders, election-policy organizations, and his own legislative work product. His Facebook page features a campaign video titled ["Kris Kobach Wanted This 20-Year-Old To Go To Jail For…"](https://www.facebook.com/PatProctorKS/videos/enforcing-our-election-laws/1920239725529443/) framing his own enforcement stance against Attorney General Kris Kobach's. A separate page post identifies him as "the chairman of your House Elections Committee and as your next Secretary of State" ([source](https://www.facebook.com/PatProctorKS/posts/as-the-chairman-of-your-house-elections-committee-and-as-your-next-secretary-of-/1227794369167664/)). An October 2025 [YouTube video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HsDMhN6Ltbs) records his endorsement of Steve Clay for Leavenworth City Commission, the only down-ballot endorsement visible in the harvested set. The harvested set contains no posts amplifying, tagging, or appearing alongside his Republican primary opponent for Secretary of State, Rep. Ken Rahjes.
signals.caveat: Candidate-controlled post or candidate-controlled platform statement; still use as stated/observed content, not inferred motive.

signals.observation: Engagement on Proctor's content is not evenly distributed. His Facebook page hosts the highest-engagement videos when they touch enforcement of election law and ballot-integrity claims, including the [Kobach-framed enforcement video](https://www.facebook.com/PatProctorKS/videos/enforcing-our-election-laws/1920239725529443/). Critical engagement is also concentrated there: the activist account [Loud Light](https://www.facebook.com/LoudLightKS) reposts and challenges his statements at video-length, including a clip titled ["Rep. Pat Proctor after being confronted at a town hall, the police are on their way"](https://www.facebook.com/LoudLightKS/videos/rep-pat-proctor-after-being-confronted-at-a-town-hall-the-police-are-on-their-wa/1516695455979360/) (captured from his April 19, 2025 Leavenworth town hall) and a second video questioning a [statement about Kansas voters](https://www.facebook.com/LoudLightKS/videos/have-you-all-heard-pat-proctor-for-kansas-secretary-of-state-latest-lie-when-he-/628564576673155/). At that April 19, 2025 town hall, asked by a constituent to explain remarks about women voters, Proctor replied, "That'd be really terrible if I'd actually said that" ([source](https://kansasreflector.com/2025/06/13/leavenworth-house-member-first-republican-to-declare-as-2026-candidate-for-secretary-of-state/)).

Candidate-controlled posts and campaign pages may be used as stated positions only when the text itself says the position.
Login-walled, blocked, or inaccessible platform content is documented as a capture limitation, not as evidence of silence.
